title: You Can Be Too Bored to Sleep - Nautilus

Boredom is more interesting than you might think. For example, it comes in a few different flavors, like state boredom, or the feeling of wanting to engage in a stimulating activity but being unable to do so. Some people are also just more prone to experiencing boredom (contrary to popular parental maxims, these aren’t necessarily “boring people”). Now, a new study published in the journal Personality and Individual Differences finds a relationship between boredom and sleep. Previous research has shown that chronic boredom is linked to difficulties with self-control. “For most people, boredom can serve as a call to action,” study author James Danckert explained in a statement. “But for people who suffer from chronic boredom, it’s very difficult to take action and can have a range of negative outcomes, from higher rates of depression and anxiety to increased drug and alcohol use, problem gambling, and problematic smartphone use.”Read more: “What Boredom Does to You”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
